Beh_F4/Trace_F4 -- General semantic slots exist; F4-specific instantiation unavailable. F3<->F4 -- Not merely untested. It is presently ill-typed as a comparison because Obs_F3 subseteq reached atoms while Obs_F4 subseteq satisfied requirements. There is no corpus-grounded mapping between these spaces.

governance.anchor: The externally supplied analysis encountered during MD-059 must not be counted as independent corroboration. MD-059 established that it: was created the same day, explicitly cited MD-058, was therefore a response to MD-058 rather than prior evidence, was classified as same-day, MD-058-consuming re-analysis. It is useful as a cross-check, but not admissible as independent corroboration of the F4 state.

lexical.anchor: I treated MD-058 and MD-059 as the frozen handover boundary and used only their recorded evidence/provenance and the primary corpus sources they explicitly relied upon. I did not perform new theory, reconciliation, model selection, F3<->F4 bridging, external literature research, or implementation. F4 is semantically instantiated in form, but not closed enough to make its satisfaction semantics computable; and it is not yet typed into a common observation space with F3. The two remaining blockers are therefore distinct: internal F4 closure and cross-model bridging.

operational.anchor: The ten Sat questions -- decisive audit: 1. Domain of K_t? K-blackboard proposed, exact structure OPEN. 2. Type of r? seven-field tuple proposed. 3. Codomain? {0,1} explicitly proposed; competing top/bot/U sub-semantics also exist. 4. Total/partial? NOT ESTABLISHED. 5. Evidence required? categories discussed, no complete evaluator. 6. Meaning of 1? requirement satisfied. 7. Meaning of 0? requirement unsatisfied. 8. Insufficient evidence? NOT CLOSED, candidate Unknown semantics exist. 9. Is UNKNOWN distinct? general theory yes, F4 Sat treatment NOT ESTABLISHED. 10. Deterministic/reproducible? NO -- no complete evaluation algorithm. Two engineers cannot currently compute the same Sat(K_t,r) from corpus-defined rules alone.

rationale_evidence.anchor: F4 completeness matrix A-K: A K_t variant census PARTIALLY FOUND (9+ mutually unreconciled variants, only 1 of 11 named components concretely typed); B component semantics NOT FOUND (only Sigma_t=(A,S,R,V,C) concretely defined, in one variant only); C relationships among variants CONFLICTING (mutually unreconciled, no component-level consistency established); D corpus-grounded common semantic core NOT FOUND; E R_t semantics PARTIALLY FOUND (Req(EC_t) exists as formal input but satisfaction predicates remain multiply defined/contested); F Sat(K_t,r) semantics PARTIALLY FOUND (shape frozen, but computing Sat requires K_t component semantics which are incomplete -- defined in form but not computationally closed); G decomposition-independent Sat NOT FOUND (the principal internal F4 blocker); H K_t->K_{t+1} transition semantics CONFLICTING (delta(K_t,e_t) and the P-12/P-13 family unresolved); I F4 Obs PARTIALLY FOUND (constructible in form, not computable); J F4 Beh PARTIALLY FOUND (general slot exists, no executable F4 Beh, classified UNAVAILABLE); K F4 Trace PARTIALLY FOUND (general machinery exists, no F4-specific instances).
rationale_evidence.statement: Gives the full eleven-item (A-K) F4 completeness matrix distinguishing what exists in form/shape from what is computationally closed across the K_t variant census, component semantics, R_t/Sat semantics, and F4's Obs/Beh/Trace, concluding this is why MD-059 did not describe F4 as simply absent -- the semantic shell is real but instantiation is incomplete.

rationale_evidence.anchor: F3<->F4 readiness matrix L-Q: L F3 observation semantics FOUND (Beh_c(K):=Reach(Ops(K)), the only candidate with real instantiated semantics); M F4 observation semantics PARTIALLY FOUND (formally constructible, not computable since Sat is not closed); N atoms<->requirements bridge NOT FOUND (F3 outputs reached atoms, F4 outputs satisfied requirements, no corpus document bridges these types); O common observation domain NOT FOUND (different codomains, no common Q,O can be posed without inventing the bridge); P common behaviour/trace domain NOT FOUND (F3 has instantiated behaviour, F4 does not); Q formal F3<->F4 equivalence relation NOT FOUND (MD-058 derived the general shape Obs-equality but not the corpus-intended ≡, and its cross-candidate matrix left all 15 pairs unresolved).
rationale_evidence.statement: Gives the full six-item (L-Q) F3<->F4 readiness matrix, establishing F3 as the only model with real instantiated observation semantics and F4 as merely formally constructible, with the critical N/O finding that F3 and F4 currently have no corpus-grounded bridge between their output types (atoms vs satisfied requirements) at all.

rationale_evidence.anchor: GA-001/GA-038 readiness R-T: R evidence sufficient for GA-001 NOT FOUND (MD-059 sharpened this to a type mismatch: atoms vs requirements); S evidence sufficient for GA-038 NOT FOUND (MD-023 found no corpus-justified canonicalization criterion, the sole positive precedent being explicit governance ratification of Delta_t, not mathematical selection); T evidence to compare F4 with another candidate beyond F3 NOT FOUND (all 15 pairwise comparisons in MD-058's matrix remained unresolved). GA-001 is blocked by missing comparable semantic types, not by lack of an equivalence formula. GA-038 is also not a hidden computational problem at present ... GA-038 cannot legitimately be marked solved merely because F4 becomes computable.
rationale_evidence.statement: Assesses both higher-level governance objectives GA-001 and GA-038 as unchanged/blocked, sharply distinguishing GA-001's blocker (a named type mismatch between atoms and requirements, not a missing equivalence formula) from GA-038's blocker (absence of any corpus-grounded canonicalization criterion, with the only successful precedent being governance ratification rather than mathematical selection), and explicitly warning that F4 becoming computable would not by itself solve GA-038.

rationale_evidence.anchor: MD-059 records: 1. reconcile the 9+ K_t variants enough to provide a decomposition-independent Sat body; 2. build the missing atoms<->requirements bridge. For the smallest fundamental blocker, the first act is prior: Research Act: establish whether the existing corpus contains sufficient evidence for a decomposition-independent Sat(K_t,r) semantics across the existing K_t variants. Without Sat, Obs_F4 is not computable. Without Obs_F4, F4 has no comparable instantiated observation semantics. Without F4 semantics, the F3<->F4 comparison cannot advance. GA-001 therefore cannot advance through F4. The atoms<->requirements bridge is a second, independent blocker, but even a perfect bridge cannot make Sat(K_t,r) computable. That research act has not been executed here.
rationale_evidence.statement: Identifies the single smallest fundamental next research act as determining whether the existing corpus already contains sufficient evidence for a decomposition-independent Sat(K_t,r) (prior to actually reconciling the 9+ K_t variants), arguing it is logically prior to the separately-needed atoms<->requirements bridge since even a perfect bridge cannot make Sat computable; explicitly states this act has not been executed in this document.

rationale_evidence.anchor: Verdicts: T FOUND-UNTYPED; delta PARTIALLY GROUNDED; tau_1..tau_11 FOUND-UNTYPED/OPEN as functions; H_t FOUND-UNTYPED; K_{t+1}=delta(K_t,e_t) as universal F4 rule NOT ESTABLISHED; Replay PROPOSED, not established as F4 semantics.
rationale_evidence.statement: Gives per-object verdicts for the six transition-related historical constructs, none reaching a closed, established F4-wide status.

rationale_evidence.anchor: F4 specificity audit (table): K_t in K-blackboard F4-SPECIFIC UNCLEAR; concrete Model-B K_t variants F4-SPECIFIC; K-blackboard GENERAL; r(K_t)=x_t GENERAL; Obs(s,W,m,c) GENERAL; EC(S,G,Q,C) GENERAL/F4-adjacent; Sat(K_t,r) F4-SPECIFIC FORM, GENERAL SEMANTIC CONTENT; R_t/Req(EC_t) F4-ADJACENT; Delta_t F4-SPECIFIC; T/delta GENERAL/MULTIPLE LINEAGES; H_t GENERAL/UNCLEAR; equiv_sem GENERAL. A historical semantic construct mentioning K_t is not automatically a Model-B aggregate/state definition.
rationale_evidence.statement: Classifies twelve historical objects by whether each is F4-specific, general, or adjacent, establishing the DDD boundary principle that a historical construct merely mentioning K_t is not automatically a Model-B aggregate/state definition.

rationale_evidence.anchor: Composition test (13 arrows): K_t -> r(K_t)=x_t DIRECT; K_t -> Obs NO EVIDENCED LINK; r(K_t)=x_t -> Obs NO EVIDENCED LINK; Obs -> EC NO EVIDENCED LINK; EC -> R_t/Req(EC_t) DIRECT but construction algorithm open; K_t+r -> Sat(K_t,r) DIRECT but only at definitional/formula level; Sat -> Delta_t DIRECT; Delta_t -> T/delta NO EVIDENCED LINK; T/delta -> H_t CORROBORATED, not closed F4-specific; H_t -> equiv_sem NO EVIDENCED LINK; r1,r2 -> equiv_sem DIRECT; Sat -> equiv_sem NO EVIDENCED LINK; Obs -> equiv_sem STRUCTURAL RESEMBLANCE. The corpus does not contain one closed semantic pipeline. It contains several genuine fragments ... but the crucial cross-links are absent. This is not merely 'one missing function.' It is a partially composed semantic system.
rationale_evidence.statement: Runs a thirteen-arrow composition test across the full semantic chain from K_t to equiv_sem, finding five DIRECT links, one CORROBORATED link, one STRUCTURAL RESEMBLANCE, and six with NO EVIDENCED LINK at all, concluding the corpus is not merely missing one function but constitutes a genuinely partially composed semantic system with several disconnected fragments.

rationale_evidence.anchor: Maximum three blockers. Blocker 1 -- K_t semantic binding: no closed mathematical type for K-blackboard and no evidence binding one concrete representation to the abstract semantic state without a modelling choice; this blocks the domain on which Sat operates. Blocker 2 -- closed satisfaction semantics: the corpus does not close evidence sufficiency, acceptance standard, temporal validity, uncertainty, model validity, insufficient-evidence treatment, or binary-vs-unknown-aware outcome semantics; this is the direct blocker to computing Sat and therefore Delta_t. Blocker 3 -- semantic composition/observable binding: the chain K_t -> r(K_t) -> Obs_F4 -> EC -> Sat -> Delta_t -> T/delta -> H_t has several explicit individual arrows but the cross-links required for a single F4 semantic system are missing; this blocks later F4 semantic equivalence and a well-typed F3<->F4 comparison.
rationale_evidence.statement: Reduces the entire historical audit to exactly three blockers: (1) no closed mathematical type for K-blackboard binding the abstract semantic state to a concrete representation, (2) no computable Sat evaluator across seven named unresolved dimensions, and (3) the missing cross-links needed to compose the individual historical fragments into one F4-specific semantic system.

rationale_evidence.anchor: The underlying predicates are themselves unresolved or multiply defined, including C_KOS, |=, Contr, >=, delta, and Qualify.
rationale_evidence.statement: Lists six further underlying predicates feeding into Sat's evaluation that are themselves unresolved or multiply defined across the corpus: C_KOS, the satisfaction/entailment relation, Contr, the epistemic ordering relation, delta, and Qualify.

rationale_evidence.anchor: semantic fragments exist =/=> semantic composition exists. The historical F4 audit reaches exactly this conclusion: F4 has the K_t, Delta_t, R_t, Sat vocabulary, but lacks a complete F4-specific observation, behaviour, trace, transition and satisfaction construction.
rationale_evidence.statement: States the composition test's core lesson as a compact non-implication (semantic fragments existing does not imply semantic composition existing), restating the shared conclusion of this document's audit series that F4 has the vocabulary but not the construction.

rationale_evidence.anchor: Requested properties for equiv_sem: operands PARTIAL; domain NOT CLOSED; codomain NOT CLOSED; criterion PARTIALLY FOUND; reflexivity NOT ESTABLISHED; symmetry NOT ESTABLISHED; transitivity NOT ESTABLISHED; equivalence classes NOT ESTABLISHED; dependence on K_t NOT CLOSED; dependence on EC NOT CLOSED; dependence on observations NOT CLOSED. Therefore this is not yet ready for actual F4 equivalence evaluation.
rationale_evidence.statement: Runs a formal eleven-property checklist against the historical semantic-equivalence relation equiv_sem, finding not even its basic equivalence-relation properties (reflexivity, symmetry, transitivity) or equivalence-class construction established, concluding it is not ready for actual F4 equivalence evaluation -- more granular than the circularity observation made in historical_source.md (S2889).

rationale_evidence.anchor: Decisive conclusion C -- Backbone is only partially composed. Not A, because Sat and semantic equivalence are not executable. Not merely B, because the principal issue is not one isolated missing type: the composition between historically grounded constructs is not established as an F4/Model-B semantic system. Not D as the primary conclusion, because although there are genuine competing formulations, the deeper finding is that the corpus has not established the relationships necessary to determine which alternatives constitute the same semantic object.
rationale_evidence.statement: Explicitly rules out three alternative conclusions (A: backbone entirely absent; B: one isolated missing type; D: the issue is merely competing formulations) in favor of conclusion C (partially composed backbone), giving explicit reasoning for excluding each alternative -- a more structured elimination argument than the parallel conclusion in historical_source.md (S2889).

rationale_evidence.anchor: F3's outputs reached atoms; F4's outputs satisfied requirements; no corpus bridge exists between those types. F3 atom -/-> F4 requirement until an evidence-grounded mapping is found. And importantly, choosing V7 would not solve this problem. It would merely give us one F4 representation against which we could attempt the mapping.
rationale_evidence.statement: Reaffirms the atoms-vs-requirements type mismatch between F3 and F4 (matching handover_verdict's N/O findings) and explicitly argues that resolving the V7-vs-canonical-K_t question would not by itself solve the F3<->F4 bridging problem -- it would only supply one candidate representation against which the still-missing mapping could be attempted.

rationale_evidence.anchor: The real bottleneck is #1+#2. At present we effectively have K_t, EC_t, r but not the missing semantic function (K_t,r,EC_t) -> Sat(K_t,r,EC_t). More specifically, we need something like EC_t -> Standard_r -> AcceptanceCondition_r -> Sat(K_t,r), with every arrow supported by corpus evidence or explicitly marked as a research proposal. Without that, we cannot legitimately compute Delta_t = {r in Req_t: not Sat(K_t,r)}. And without Delta_t, the whole Zero/adequacy machinery remains underdetermined.
rationale_evidence.statement: Identifies the combined bottleneck (gaps #1+#2) as the missing semantic function (K_t,r,EC_t)->Sat, decomposed into a required four-stage chain EC_t -> Standard_r -> AcceptanceCondition_r -> Sat(K_t,r), arguing that without it Delta_t cannot be legitimately computed and the entire Zero/adequacy machinery remains underdetermined.

rationale_evidence.anchor: Even if tomorrow we solved Sat(K_t,r) we still would not automatically have F3<->F4. We would still need a structure-preserving correspondence Atoms_F3 <-> Requirements_F4, including the semantics of what an atom contributes to requirement satisfaction. Solving the first does not solve the second. F4 internal semantics (EC->Standard->Accept->Sat, typed K_t) and F3<->F4 (atom->requirement correspondence) are two separate problems.
rationale_evidence.statement: Argues gap #4 (F3<->F4 bridging) is genuinely independent of gap #1/#2 (F4 internal semantics): solving Sat would not automatically produce the required structure-preserving Atoms_F3<->Requirements_F4 correspondence, since these are two separate problems with distinct dependency trees.

## Notes for P3
This is one of the corpus's largest and most disciplined single-day research audits (S2888 through S2903, 2026-09), and its CONTESTED lifecycle flag reflects real, explicitly-diagnosed internal corpus conflicts rather than any confusion within the audit itself — the audit's entire purpose is to locate and precisely characterize exactly these conflicts (the K_t abstract/concrete conflict, the "r" notation collision, the four incompatible transition-semantics formulations, and the three incompatible equiv_sem candidates) without resolving them, since resolution was explicitly out of scope for this handover. P3 should note the audit series is remarkably self-disciplined about provenance: it repeatedly distinguishes corpus-native findings from same-day constructed candidates (MD-061's `Sat*`, `Accept_r`, `Req_Sigma`, V7) and explicitly refuses to let a later document's convenient restatement count as independent corroboration of an earlier one. The single most load-bearing finding for future work is MD-062's result (row 81, S2896): MD-061's requirement shape never actually takes `EC_t` as an argument, meaning the "Requirement-Evaluation Semantic Boundary" (not Sat itself) is the true remaining blocker — this finding is independently re-confirmed and sharpened across Documents 8 and 9 (S2896, S2897) and should be treated as this label's most load-bearing single claim. Given the low group-membership count here (only 3 CO-OCCURRENCE groups, no POSSIBLY-relations), P3's main task for this label is likely internal (verifying the chain of 15 sub-documents holds together) rather than resolving identity questions against other labels.
